request_state.title: KRAUS SIEVE MODULAR METHOD EXTENSION FOR SIGNATURE (3, 3, p) ON [5201, 5300]
request_state.claim: No non-trivial primitive solutions exist for signature (3, 3, p) for all prime exponents p in [5201, 5300].
request_state.method: Modular method level lowering to conductor 72, Kraus sieve relations at auxiliary primes q = 2kp + 1 with a_q(f) = 0 mod 2.

relevance.instructions: How directly does this candidate address the general Beal conjecture across arbitrary triples (p, q, r) >= 3?
criteria: level 0: Settles only bounded prime exponents or dead category computation with no general leverage.
level 1: Relevant to a single signature family or requires bounded bad reduction.
level 2: Provides structural constraints applicable to infinite families with unbounded exponents.
level 3: Directly attacks the general Beal conjecture for all (p, q, r) >= 3 via uniform Diophantine geometry.

fc_blindness.instructions: Is this candidate's mathematical mechanism blind to exponent 2 (i.e. does it also hold for Fermat-Catalan identities with exponent 2)?

criteria.true: The mechanism holds on all Fermat-Catalan identities with exponent 2, hence cannot prove Beal on its own.
criteria.false: The mechanism strictly exploits the Beal hyperbolic defect -chi >= 1/12 (which fails on Fermat-Catalan) or specific exponent >= 3 geometry.

dead_category.instructions: Does this candidate fall into a known dead category (bounded sieves, modular method one signature at a time, elementary congruences, abc/Baker)?

criteria.true: Yes, it is in a known dead category incapable of proving the full conjecture.
criteria.false: No, it explores live directions such as effective Diophantine geometry on orbifolds or unifying motivic objects.
